title: Moharram Ali v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J. and Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; fresh theft-dues order must follow Supply Code procedure.
headnote: Where the Electricity Department withdraws a demand notice for recovery of dues alleged to arise from theft of electricity and states that a fresh order will follow the procedure prescribed in law, the writ challenging that notice is disposed of with liberty to pass the fresh order strictly in accordance with the procedure under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court did not examine the demand on merits and cited no numbered clause.
facts: Moharram Ali petitioned the Allahabad High Court against a demand notice dated 2 September 2022 issued by the respondent Electricity Department for recovery of electricity dues said to arise from theft of electricity. On 23 February 2023 the Court granted the Department time to obtain instructions and listed the writ afresh. On 1 March 2023 counsel for the Department stated that the impugned recovery had been withdrawn and that a fresh order would be passed after the procedure prescribed in law.

holding_units.topic: Fresh order after withdrawal of a theft-dues recovery
holding_units.holding: Once the distribution licensee withdraws a demand notice for recovery of electricity dues in a case of theft and states that a fresh order will be passed after following the procedure prescribed in law, the writ challenging that notice is disposed of with liberty to the licensee to pass the fresh order strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
holding_units.flag: No numbered clause is cited. The order refers only to the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Applied to dispose the writ after the Department withdrew the 2 September 2022 theft-dues recovery, leaving any fresh order to be passed strictly in accordance with the procedure under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, without a merits decision.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand notice dated 2 September 2022 was a lawful assessment of theft dues, and what a fresh order may determine.
not_decided.note: The Court recorded the Department's withdrawal and did not rule on the assessment. It identified no Supply Code clause governing the fresh order.
